2. Relevant facts are that respondent No. 1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 106 of 1992 before the Assistant Judge, Kaliakoir, Dhaka for declaration of title to 'C' schedule land which he acquired by auction-purchase in a certificate sale and also by inheritance from the father alleging that Kasimuddin and Ibrahim owned and possessed 7.26 acres of land in 14 different plots under CS Khatian No. 42, Mouza Galachipa, PS Savar, Dhaka. Ibrahim subsequently by amicable arrangement possessed 3.96 acres of land. He thereafter mortgaged 3.67 acres of land to Trailankhya Mohan Rakshit who eventually foreclosed the mortgage in Mortgage Suit No. (39/1926)/ (928/1927) against the heirs and successors of Ibrahim and obtained preliminary decree on 9-3-1927 and final decree on 25-4-1927. Thereafter, Trailankhya Mohan Rakshit orally gifted 3.56 acres of land to his sister Suniti Bala Datta who in turn sold 0.47 acres of land in plot No. 557 to Ramjan Ali, predecessor-in-interest of defendant Nos. 3-8 and 0.67 acres of land in plot No. 794 to Hazrat Ali, Hasenuddin and Hikmat Ali and delivered possession. 

 3. Subsequent to the mortgage of the land to Trailankhya Mohan Rakshit, Ibrahim sold 4.58 acres of land including the said mortgaged land of CS Khatian No. 42 to Sk Rahimuddin, Sk. Tamijuddin, father of the plaintiff, Sk. Dagu, Makim Ali and Mohar Ali and delivered possession. After the death of his father, the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 became the owner of the land owned by his father and continued possessing the same jointly with other defendants.
